subproblems.title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm: continuity and comparison with the operator norm
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers m, k: the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2 (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, the standard basis of R^m) is a continuous function of A on the space of continuous linear maps R^m -> R^k with the operator-norm topology; and for every such A: 0 <= hsNormSq(A), hsNormSq(A) <= m ||A||^2 where ||A|| is the operator norm, and |A v|^2 <= hsNormSq(A) |v|^2 for every v in R^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k : ℕ), Continuous (fun A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k => hsNormSq A) ∧ ∀ A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k, 0 ≤ hsNormSq A ∧ hsNormSq A ≤ m * ‖A‖ ^ 2 ∧ ∀ v : Rn m, ‖A v‖ ^ 2 ≤ hsNormSq A * ‖v‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not needed for the argument): these are the Hilbert-Schmidt facts the parent node and its siblings plane_tilt_comparison and plane_dist_transfer need (continuity of hsNormSq and hsNormSq A <= m ||A||^2 for integrability; ||A v||^2 <= hsNormSq A ||v||^2 for the operator bound; 0 <= hsNormSq A). Exact reuse of the comparator-accepted declaration lgc_hsNormSq_bounds (node root.lipschitz_graph_corollary-a1.hole_estimate-a1.hs_norm_bounds-a1, accepted candidate commit 7372f81c6640dd17bd99bd3c9bbe79675f27d126) with its identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i in Fin m; these vectors form the standard orthonormal basis of R^m, so |e_i| = 1. For v in R^m, v_i denotes its i-th coordinate. By definition hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < m of |A e_i|^2. ||A|| is the operator norm of A : R^m ->L R^k.

1. Continuity. Fix i. The evaluation map A -> A e_i is linear in A and satisfies |A e_i - B e_i| = |(A - B) e_i| <= ||A - B|| |e_i| = ||A - B||, so it is continuous for the operator-norm topology. Composing with the continuous maps w -> |w| and t -> t^2 gives a continuous real function A -> |A e_i|^2. A finite sum of continuous real functions is continuous, so A -> sum_i |A e_i|^2 = hsNormSq(A) is continuous.
2. Nonnegativity. Every summand |A e_i|^2 is >= 0, hence hsNormSq(A) >= 0.
3. Upper bound by the operator norm. For each i, 0 <= |A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A||, so |A e_i|^2 <= ||A||^2. Summing over the m indices gives hsNormSq(A) <= sum_{i<m} ||A||^2 = m ||A||^2.
4. Coordinates. Every v in R^m satisfies v = sum_i v_i e_i, because the j-th coordinate of the right side is sum_i v_i delta_{ij} = v_j. For the Euclidean norm, |v|^2 = sum_i v_i^2 = sum_i |v_i|^2.
5. Bound on |A v|. By linearity of A and step 4, A v = sum_i v_i (A e_i). The triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm give |A v| <= sum_i |v_i (A e_i)| = sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|.
6. Cauchy-Schwarz. For finite sums of real numbers, (sum_i a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum_i a_i^2)(sum_i b_i^2). With a_i = |v_i| and b_i = |A e_i| and step 4, (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= (sum_i |v_i|^2)(sum_i |A e_i|^2) = |v|^2 hsNormSq(A).
7. Conclusion. Since 0 <= |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i| (step 5), squaring preserves the inequality, and step 6 gives |A v|^2 <= (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= hsNormSq(A) |v|^2. If m = 0, all sums are empty and v = 0, so each assertion reads 0 <= 0 and the steps above apply verbatim. QED

Lean notes (names that worked under the pinned toolchain): unfold hsNormSq, then fun_prop (step 1) and positivity (step 2); ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and the norm of EuclideanSpace.single (step 3); ext with simp [Pi.single_apply] (step 4); map_sum, map_smul, norm_sum_le, norm_smul (step 5); Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq and EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq (step 6).
proof_key_steps: Continuity: each evaluation A -> A e_i is continuous linear, and hsNormSq is a finite sum of squared norms of such maps
Nonnegativity: hsNormSq A is a sum of squares
|A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A||; summing over i < m gives hsNormSq A <= m ||A||^2
Expand v = sum_i v_i e_i; linearity and the triangle inequality give |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|
Cauchy-Schwarz gives (sum_i |v_i| |A e_i|)^2 <= |v|^2 hsNormSq A; squaring the nonnegative bound gives |A v|^2 <= hsNormSq A |v|^2

subproblems.title: Distance to a plane is controlled by the distance to a nearby plane
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, P and Q linear subspaces of R^{n+l} with orthogonal projections p_P = P.starProjection and p_Q = Q.starProjection, and x in R^{n+l}. Then dist(x, P) <= dist(x, Q) + hsNorm(p_P - p_Q) ||x||, where dist(x, S) = infDist x S and hsNorm is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm A = sqrt(hsNormSq A), hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (P Q : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)) (x : Amb n ℓ), infDist x (P : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ infDist x (Q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) + hsNorm (P.starProjection - Q.starProjection) * ‖x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not needed for the argument): extracted from the parent node's proof, where it bounds the distance from the support to the plane T by the distance to the affine-approximation plane T~ plus hsNorm(p_T - p_T~) ||x||; here it is stated for arbitrary subspaces P, Q and an arbitrary point x. The argument below is self-contained.

Notation. N := n + l, so R^{n+l} = EuclideanSpace R (Fin N). A := p_P - p_Q, a continuous linear map R^N -> R^N. Every linear subspace S of R^N is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so its orthogonal projection p_S = S.starProjection exists, and p_S y lies in S for every y.

1. Operator bound by the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. By the sibling lemma hs_norm_bounds (lgc_hsNormSq_bounds) with m = k = N applied to A: 0 <= hsNormSq A and ||A x||^2 <= hsNormSq A * ||x||^2. The square root is monotone on [0, oo), and sqrt(t^2) = t for t >= 0, sqrt(a b) = sqrt(a) sqrt(b) for a >= 0. Hence ||A x|| = sqrt(||A x||^2) <= sqrt(hsNormSq A * ||x||^2) = sqrt(hsNormSq A) * sqrt(||x||^2) = hsNorm A * ||x||.
2. Nearest-point property. For every subspace S of R^N and every y, the orthogonal projection p_S y is a nearest point of S to y, so dist(y, p_S y) = infDist(y, S) (Mathlib: Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist). With dist(y, w) = ||y - w|| this gives infDist(x, P) = ||x - p_P x|| and infDist(x, Q) = ||x - p_Q x||.
3. Decomposition. x - p_P x = (x - p_Q x) - (p_P x - p_Q x) = (x - p_Q x) - A x, because (p_P - p_Q) x = p_P x - p_Q x. By the triangle inequality ||u - v|| <= ||u|| + ||v||: ||x - p_P x|| <= ||x - p_Q x|| + ||A x||.
4. Conclusion. By steps 2, 3 and 1: infDist(x, P) = ||x - p_P x|| <= ||x - p_Q x|| + ||A x|| = infDist(x, Q) + ||A x|| <= infDist(x, Q) + hsNorm(p_P - p_Q) * ||x||. QED

Lean notes (names that worked under the pinned toolchain; a complete proof of the frozen type was compiled in this decomposition session): have hb := (lgc_hsNormSq_bounds (n + ℓ) (n + ℓ)).2 (P.starProjection - Q.starProjection); for step 1 unfold hsNorm and rewrite with Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _) (twice) and Real.sqrt_mul hb.1, then Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (hb.2.2 x); for step 2 rw [← P.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist x, ← Q.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist x, dist_eq_norm, dist_eq_norm]; step 3 by congr 1; simp only [FunLike.coe_sub, Pi.sub_apply]; abel, then norm_sub_le and gcongr.
proof_key_steps: ||(p_P - p_Q) x|| <= hsNorm(p_P - p_Q) ||x|| by taking square roots in ||A x||^2 <= hsNormSq A ||x||^2 (hs_norm_bounds)
infDist(x, S) = ||x - p_S x|| for S = P, Q (the orthogonal projection is a nearest point)
x - p_P x = (x - p_Q x) - (p_P - p_Q) x and the triangle inequality
combine: infDist(x, P) <= infDist(x, Q) + hsNorm(p_P - p_Q) ||x||

subproblems.title: Mass-weighted comparison of two planes by their tilt-excess on a ball
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U any subset of R^{n+l}, and V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu = V.weight such that x |-> V.tangentProj x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Let z in R^{n+l} and s > 0 with mu(B_s(z)) < oo (closed ball). Then for all linear subspaces P, Q of R^{n+l}: mu(B_s(z)) * hsNormSq(p_P - p_Q) <= 2 s^n (E(z, s, P) + E(z, s, Q)), where mu(B_s(z)) is taken as a real number (ENNReal.toReal), p_S = S.starProjection, hsNormSq is the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm and E = V.tiltExcess, E(z, s, S) = s^{-n} * integral over B_s(z) of hsNormSq(V.tangentProj x - p_S) dmu.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → V.weight (closedBall z s) ≠ ⊤ → ∀ P Q : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), (V.weight (closedBall z s)).toReal * hsNormSq (P.starProjection - Q.starProjection) ≤ 2 * s ^ n * (V.tiltExcess z s P + V.tiltExcess z s Q)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not needed for the argument): extracted from the parent node's proof, where it is used with z = 0, s = delta rho, P = T and Q = T~ (the plane from affine approximation); here it is stated for an arbitrary centre z, radius s and subspaces P, Q. The argument below is self-contained.

Notation. B := B_s(z) (closed ball); mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; for a subspace R of R^{n+l}, p_R := R.starProjection and phi_R(x) := hsNormSq(p_x - p_R); w := mu(B).toReal; N := n + l. By hypothesis mu(B) is finite. We use the sibling lemma hs_norm_bounds (lgc_hsNormSq_bounds) with m = k = N: the map A |-> hsNormSq A is continuous, and 0 <= hsNormSq A <= N ||A||^2 for every continuous linear A : R^N -> R^N.

1. Operator norms of the projections. For every x, ||p_x|| <= 1: by definition V.tangentProj x is either the orthogonal projection (Classical.choose h).starProjection onto some subspace, whose operator norm is <= 1 (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le), or the zero map, of norm 0 <= 1. Likewise ||p_R|| <= 1 for every subspace R.
2. Integrability. Fix a subspace R. (a) The map x |-> p_x - p_R is mu-a.e. strongly measurable (the difference of the mu-a.e. strongly measurable map x |-> p_x, a hypothesis, and a constant), and hsNormSq is continuous, so phi_R = hsNormSq o (x |-> p_x - p_R) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. (b) For every x, |phi_R(x)| = phi_R(x) <= N ||p_x - p_R||^2 <= N (||p_x|| + ||p_R||)^2 <= N * 2^2 = 4N, by nonnegativity, the bound of hs_norm_bounds, the triangle inequality and step 1. (c) A mu-a.e. strongly measurable real function that is bounded by a constant on a set of finite mu-measure is integrable on that set (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with mu(B) != oo). Hence phi_R is mu-integrable on B, in particular for R = P and R = Q.
3. Pointwise inequality. Fix x. For each standard basis vector e_i of R^N put a := (p_x - p_Q) e_i and b := (p_x - p_P) e_i. Then (p_P - p_Q) e_i = p_P e_i - p_Q e_i = a - b. By the triangle inequality and 2 ||a|| ||b|| <= ||a||^2 + ||b||^2, ||a - b||^2 <= (||a|| + ||b||)^2 <= 2 ||a||^2 + 2 ||b||^2. Summing over i = 1, ..., N (definition hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2) gives hsNormSq(p_P - p_Q) <= 2 hsNormSq(p_x - p_P) + 2 hsNormSq(p_x - p_Q) = 2 phi_P(x) + 2 phi_Q(x).
4. Integration. The constant function c := hsNormSq(p_P - p_Q) is integrable on B (B has finite measure), and its integral over B is mu(B).toReal * c = w c (setIntegral_const; mu.real B = mu(B).toReal). The function 2 phi_P + 2 phi_Q is integrable on B by step 2. By step 3 and monotonicity of the integral, w c <= integral over B of (2 phi_P + 2 phi_Q) dmu = 2 * integral_B phi_P dmu + 2 * integral_B phi_Q dmu (linearity of the integral for integrable functions).
5. Rewriting with the tilt-excess. Since s > 0, s^n != 0, and by the definition E(z, s, R) = (s^n)^{-1} * integral_B phi_R dmu we get s^n E(z, s, R) = integral_B phi_R dmu for R = P, Q. Therefore 2 integral_B phi_P dmu + 2 integral_B phi_Q dmu = 2 s^n E(z, s, P) + 2 s^n E(z, s, Q) = 2 s^n (E(z, s, P) + E(z, s, Q)).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give mu(B_s(z)).toReal * hsNormSq(p_P - p_Q) <= 2 s^n (E(z, s, P) + E(z, s, Q)). QED

subproblems.title: Affine approximation at the origin at scale 2 delta rho: a plane of small tilt and small height (Simon 4.5 proof, the plane T~ = T(0, 2 sigma))
subproblems.statement: Assume the contract Prop AffineApproximationLemma (Simon 2.5). For n >= 1, l and p > n there is C > 0, depending only on n, l, p, with the property: if U is open, V is a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U, H : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l}, 0 < delta <= 1/4, AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold, and K(0, 2 delta rho) <= delta, where K(y, r) = V.scaledLpNorm H p y r = (r^{p-n} int_{B_r(y)} |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} in [0, oo], then there is an n-dimensional subspace T with E(0, delta rho, T) <= C (delta^gamma)^2 and dist(x, T) <= C delta^gamma (delta rho) for all x in spt V cap B_{2 delta rho}(0) (closed balls), where gamma = 1/(2n+2), E = V.tiltExcess and dist(x, T) = infDist x T.
subproblems.lean_statement: AffineApproximationLemma → ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 / 4 → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → V.scaledLpNorm H p 0 (2 * (δ * ρ)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ → ∃ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n ∧ V.tiltExcess 0 (δ * ρ) T ≤ C * (δ ^ (1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 2))) ^ 2 ∧ ∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (2 * (δ * ρ)), infDist x (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ C * δ ^ (1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 2)) * (δ * ρ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (not needed for the argument): extracted from the parent node's proof (the plane T~ = T(0, 2 delta rho) of Simon's proof of 4.5, steps (1), (2)). The bound K(0, 2 delta rho) <= delta is a hypothesis here; the parent derives it from its own dependency on the scaled L^p bounds. The single constant C below dominates both constants 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 (tilt) and 2 C_A (height) used in the parent proof. The argument below is self-contained.

Notation. gamma := 1/(2n+2); sigma := delta rho; mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; p_P := P.starProjection; g := delta^gamma (real rpow); heightSup(xi, r, P) := V.heightSup xi r P = sup over x in spt V cap B_r(xi) of ofReal(infDist(x - xi, P)) in [0, oo]; K(y, r) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y r; E(xi, r, P) := V.tiltExcess xi r P = (r^n)^{-1} * integral over B_r(xi) of hsNormSq(p_x - p_P) dmu. ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal.
Constants. Let C_A > 0 be the constant that AffineApproximationLemma provides for (n, l, p) (it depends only on n, l, p). Put C := 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 + 2 C_A. Then C > 0 and C depends only on n, l, p.
Fix U open, V, H, delta, rho with 0 < delta <= 1/4, AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, and K(0, 2 sigma) <= ofReal delta.

1. Preliminaries. AllardHypotheses give rho > 0 and 0 in spt V. Hence sigma = delta rho > 0, and 0 in spt V cap B_sigma(0) because ||0|| = 0 <= sigma. Also g = delta^gamma >= 0 (rpow of a nonnegative base).
2. delta <= g. As n >= 1, 2n + 2 >= 4 > 0, so 0 < gamma <= 1. Because 0 < delta <= 1/4 <= 1, the map t |-> delta^t is nonincreasing on R, so delta = delta^1 <= delta^gamma = g.
3. Affine approximation. Apply AffineApproximationLemma (with U open, 0 < delta <= 1/4 and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho) at xi := 0, which lies in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0) by step 1, with radius sigma_2 := 2 sigma = 2 (delta rho); indeed 0 < sigma_2 and sigma_2 = 2 * delta * rho, so sigma_2 <= 2 delta rho. It yields a subspace T with finrank T = n and
 (a) ofReal(C_A^{-1} sqrt((sigma_2^n)^{-1} * integral over B_{sigma_2/2}(0) of hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) dmu)) <= ofReal(sigma_2^{-1}) * heightSup(0, sigma_2, T) + K(0, sigma_2),
 (b) ofReal(sigma_2^{-1}) * heightSup(0, sigma_2, T) <= ofReal(C_A g).
 Since sigma_2/2 = sigma, the integral in (a) is J := integral over B_sigma(0) of hsNormSq(p_x - p_T) dmu. We take this T; it has dimension n.
4. Tilt bound. (i) J >= 0: hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2 >= 0 for every A, and the (Bochner) integral of a pointwise nonnegative function is >= 0 whether or not it is integrable. (ii) By (b), the hypothesis K(0, 2 sigma) <= ofReal delta and step 2 (ofReal is monotone), the right side of (a) is <= ofReal(C_A g) + ofReal(g) = ofReal(C_A g + g) = ofReal((C_A + 1) g), using ofReal(a) + ofReal(b) = ofReal(a + b) for a, b >= 0. (iii) Hence ofReal(C_A^{-1} sqrt(((2 sigma)^n)^{-1} J)) <= ofReal((C_A + 1) g); as (C_A + 1) g >= 0, this is equivalent to C_A^{-1} sqrt(((2 sigma)^n)^{-1} J) <= (C_A + 1) g (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), and multiplying by C_A > 0 gives sqrt(((2 sigma)^n)^{-1} J) <= C_A (C_A + 1) g. (iv) Since C_A (C_A + 1) g >= 0, sqrt(a) <= b is equivalent to a <= b^2, so ((2 sigma)^n)^{-1} J <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 g^2. (v) Since (2 sigma)^n = 2^n sigma^n and sigma > 0, E(0, sigma, T) = (sigma^n)^{-1} J = 2^n ((2 sigma)^n)^{-1} J <= 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 g^2 <= C g^2, the last step because 2 C_A g^2 >= 0. This is E(0, delta rho, T) <= C (delta^gamma)^2.
5. Height bound. Let x in spt V cap B_{2 sigma}(0). (i) ofReal(infDist(x, T)) = ofReal(infDist(x - 0, T)) <= heightSup(0, 2 sigma, T), because it is one of the terms of the supremum (le_iSup₂). (ii) Multiplying by ofReal((2 sigma)^{-1}) (monotone multiplication in [0, oo]) and using (b): ofReal((2 sigma)^{-1}) * ofReal(infDist(x, T)) <= ofReal(C_A g); since (2 sigma)^{-1} >= 0, the left side equals ofReal((2 sigma)^{-1} infDist(x, T)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). (iii) As C_A g >= 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff gives (2 sigma)^{-1} infDist(x, T) <= C_A g, i.e. infDist(x, T) <= 2 C_A g sigma (multiply by 2 sigma > 0). (iv) 2 C_A <= C because 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 >= 0, and g sigma >= 0, so infDist(x, T) <= C g sigma = C delta^gamma (delta rho).
6. T has dimension n and satisfies both bounds, with C depending only on n, l, p. QED
